Society & Human Rights
• Hundreds of thousands protested across France for a range of social and economic grievances; police made over 1,300 arrests and used gas to disperse student crowds, while solidarity demonstrations spread from Milan and Rome to Madrid, Lisbon and Tirana.
• Thousands of Northern Irish Protestant Orange Order members marched in Portadown ahead of a court ruling, highlighting persistent tensions around parading rights.
• A mounting dispute over conscription of Israel’s ultra-Orthodox community could destabilize Prime Minister Netanyahu’s coalition.
• In Africa, small businesses spotlighted losses from employee theft, while Ukraine said Starlink service returned to normal after disruptions, underscoring the social stakes of connectivity.
Why it matters: From Europe’s streets to Israel and Northern Ireland, social strains and governance challenges are testing institutions’ ability to defuse unrest and maintain public trust.

Why it matters: Control over critical tech infrastructure and closely fought elections from Brazil to Israel are shaping geopolitical alignments and policy choices with global spillovers.

Why it matters: Slowing consumer demand, bond market volatility and shifting capital flows are reordering risks and leadership choices across sectors and regions.

Entertainment.title: Marvel’s Real-Gem Infinity Gauntlet Is Up for Grabs — If You Can Get Approved to Bid
Entertainment.text: SummaryThe one-of-one Marvel Infinity Gauntlet replica set with real gemstones is heading to auction for the first time this DecemberEach of its six gems stands in for an Infinity Stone, and none of them has been treated or enhancedThe piece will tour Bahrain throughout November before going under the hammer in Abu DhabiThe Marvel Infinity Gauntlet replica created by East Continental Gems is set to be auctioned this December, marking the first time the one-of-one piece has been offered for sale. Built using the same design files behind the gauntlet seen on screen, the commission swaps the film prop’s fictional stones for six real gems, each matched to one of the Infinity Stones.The gems are what separate this gauntlet from every other replica on the market. Most stones sold today have undergone some form of treatment to improve their color or clarity, but all six set into this piece are untouched, a combination Julien’s Auctions suggests may not come together again. The standout is the emerald chosen for the Time Stone, a gem first unearthed more than 100 years ago that East Continental Gems kept in its own collection for over three decades and repeatedly refused to sell before releasing it for this project.The construction is rooted in Marvel’s own blueprints. The studio opened up the layered design files behind the screen-used gauntlet, allowing East Continental Gems to reproduce the prop’s form faithfully while substituting precious stones for the props’ fabricated ones. The New York jeweler, a family business working out of the same office since 1972, handled the task of translating each fictional stone into a real-world counterpart.The project traces back to 2019, when East Continental Gems CEO Adam Mirzoeff noticed a toy Infinity Gauntlet sitting on a senior Marvel executive’s desk and floated the idea, mostly as a joke, of making a real one. The finished piece was later shown publicly at San Diego Comic-Con in 2022.The gauntlet will serve as a headline lot of Julien’s Auctions’ Celebrity & Culture Experience, with the sale itself titled Pop Culture Legends. “Presenting it in Abu Dhabi, as part of Pop Culture Legends auction, gives it a stage worthy of what it is: a true 1-of-1,” Julien’s Auctions CEO Ken Citron said in a statement. Before the sale, the piece will travel to Bahrain for a tour running through November.Getting a paddle for this lot takes more than registering. Julien’s Auctions requires every bidder to be pre-approved, and the house is urging interested collectors to reach out early to discuss the gauntlet and begin that vetting process.The 1-of-1 Marvel Infinity Gauntlet goes under the hammer December 8 at Julien’s Auctions’ Pop Culture Legends sale at Rosewood Abu Dhabi, with bidder pre-approval required.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: The Square-Toe Nike Air Force 1 Low “Triple Black” Is Arriving This November
Entertainment.text: Name:  Nike Air Force 1 Low Square Toe “Triple Black”Colorway: Black/BlackSKU: JF7766-001MSRP: $130 USDRelease Date: November 6Where to Buy: NikeThe Nike Air Force 1 Low Square Toe “Triple Black” isolates its redesign to a single zone, reshaping the front of the shoe while leaving the familiar blacked-out AF1 Low largely intact. Viewed from behind or in profile at the heel, the pair reads as the same tonal sneaker that has filled closets for decades, and the real story only reveals itself at the forefoot.The toe box is where Nike made its move, pushing the front of the shoe farther forward and swapping the trademark curve for a straight leading edge framed by angular corners. The effect is most dramatic from a top-down view, where the outline shifts from soft and rounded to something closer to a squared silhouette, giving the low-top a longer, more architectural stance.Everything behind that modification sticks to the standard recipe. The upper is cut from black leather in the same monochrome treatment as the regular “Triple Black,” and the remaining panels and proportions follow the classic Air Force 1 Low blueprint, so the new front end carries the entire visual change on its own.That restraint is what makes the release worth a second look. By editing one element instead of overhauling the whole silhouette, Nike shows how much a single shape adjustment can alter a sneaker this familiar, and anyone hoping for a ground-up rethink should know the updates stay confined to the forefoot.The square-toe treatment also extends to a “Triple White” pair launching in tandem, so both of the AF1’s best-known monochrome colorways get the reworked shape. Each keeps its palette strictly tonal, letting the new toe do the talking.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.text: SummaryThe Gilded Age returns for an eight-episode fourth season, with the Russell family facing the fallout of Bertha’s social ascentCity of God: The Fight Rages On picks up its second season as rival factions battle for control after a drug lord’s deathNew documentaries from Dawn Porter, Ben Proudfoot and Rachel Fleit arrive alongside a deep bench of holiday classicsHBO Max opens its November lineup with The Gilded Age Season 4, bringing Julian Fellowes’ Gilded Age New York saga back for eight new episodes. The premiere lands November 1, kicking off a month that also delivers a second season of City of God: The Fight Rages On, four new HBO Original documentaries and A24’s Tony.Season 4 finds the Russells dealing with the price of Bertha’s hard-won place at the top of New York Society. Agnes van Rhijn spots a chance to claw back her own standing, Marian sets off in a new direction, and Peggy tries to earn the approval of the family she’s about to marry into. Carrie Coon, Christine Baranski, Cynthia Nixon, Morgan Spector, Louisa Jacobson, Denée Benton and Audra McDonald lead a sprawling ensemble that also features Bill Camp and Phylicia Rashad. Salli Richardson-Whitfield directs and executive produces, with episodes rolling out weekly on Sundays and a companion season of The Gilded Age Podcast arriving the same day.The drama shifts from ballrooms to the favelas on November 8, when City of God: The Fight Rages On returns for six episodes shot across Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo. With drug lord Curió dead, a violent scramble for the territory takes hold. Councilwoman Berenice (Roberta Rodrigues) squares off against corruption and an expanding militia, lawyer Jerusa (Andréia Horta) pursues the people who tore her family apart, and Leka (Luellem de Castro) rallies the neighborhood through funk music and dance parties. Entertainment.title: The NEEDLES x Pendleton Collection Puts Six Pieces of Archival Wool to Work
Entertainment.text: SummaryNEEDLES and Pendleton link up for the first time on a six-piece capsule cut from Pendleton’s traditional plaids and wool fabricsA boxy shirt, a jacket with leather elbow patches and a coat in an archival Pendleton pattern lead the outerwear and shirtingPlaid trousers, a mohair sweater in Pendleton’s signature Native-inspired motif and a fully lined Cowichan knit round out the lineupNEEDLES is teaming up with Pendleton for the first time, debuting a six-piece NEEDLES x Pendleton collection that reworks the American mill’s classic plaids and wool cloth. Every garment starts from Pendleton’s fabric vocabulary, then gets recut through NEEDLES’ lens across shirting, tailoring, trousers and knits. The result is a tight capsule where the textiles do the talking and the construction choices tell you how each piece is meant to be worn.The shirt sets the foundation for the collection with a relaxed, boxy silhouette that gives the plaid wool room to drape rather than cling. That easy cut turns a traditional flannel-weight top into something closer to a light overshirt, built for layering through the colder months. The jacket builds on the same fabric language but adds leather patches at the elbows, a reinforcement detail that nods to hard-wearing workwear and protects one of the first areas to wear through on a wool garment.The coat is the statement piece of the drop, cut from a pattern pulled directly from Pendleton’s archive. Pairing that historical print with a full-length outer layer gives the design the most surface area to show off, making it the clearest showcase of the partnership’s archival focus. Plaid trousers complete the tailoring side, carrying the check pattern from top to bottom so the pieces can be worn as a coordinated set or broken up across a look.The knitwear leans into texture and structure. Pendleton’s staple Native-inspired pattern appears on a sweater knit with mohair, which brings a soft, slightly brushed hand and extra warmth to the fiber blend. The Cowichan sweater, a chunky knit style with deep roots in outdoor dressing, gets a full lining throughout, a finishing step that smooths the interior against the skin and adds an extra layer of insulation.The NEEDLES x Pendleton collection is available at Nepenthes stores and the Nepenthes online store.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: The Nike Air Max 90 “Light Orewood Brown” Is All Patent Shine and See-Through Panels
Entertainment.text: Name: Nike Air Max 90 “Light Orewood Brown”Colorway: Light Orewood Brown/Blue Tint-Sail-Neutral OliveSKU: IX8056-104MSRP: $145 USDRelease Date: November 1Where to Buy: NikeNike is giving the Air Max 90 a material-driven makeover with the “Light Orewood Brown” colorway, pairing translucent overlays with high-gloss patent leather. The palette stays deliberately muted, sticking mostly to Light Orewood Brown and Sail so that texture and transparency become the main event. The result is a quiet take on Tinker Hatfield’s runner that rewards a closer look.The upper is built in layers that play off one another. Textured mesh forms the base across the toe box and collar, while translucent panels sweep along the sidewalls and frame the lacing system, letting the mesh show through from beneath. Down low, the mudguards are finished in glossy beige patent leather, adding shine and contrast without breaking from the tonal color scheme.Nike carries the see-through concept into the branding as well. The tongue labels and heel tabs are rendered in the same clear material, so the logos underneath remain visible through a glassy top layer. Cream laces and a matching lining keep the interior and lacing in step with the exterior, while a tonal midsole houses the silhouette’s signature visible Air unit in the heel.Underfoot, a semi-translucent outsole continues the theme from top to bottom. The standout accessory is a metallic Swoosh hangtag clipped to the laces, engraved with an intricate pattern that is echoed on the printed insoles. That artwork links the pair to a wider set of releases, with forthcoming Air Max 95 and Air Force 1 styles set to carry the same engraved motif alongside their own patent leather and translucent details.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: White Mountaineering x Alpha Industries Splice Three Military Classics Into Two Hybrid Jackets
Entertainment.text: SummaryWhite Mountaineering and ALPHA INDUSTRIES return for a third collaboration, built around two military-derived outerwear stylesA hybrid coat starts from the N-3B and borrows details from the MA-1 and CWU-45P, while a hybrid flight jacket pairs an MA-1 silhouette with N-3B elementsBoth styles combine water-repellent, high-density shells with a breathable, windproof WINDSTOPPER liningWhite Mountaineering and Alpha Industries have reunited for their third collaboration, a two-piece outerwear release that blends the American military outfitter’s archive with the Japanese label’s functional design. Rather than reissuing a single classic, each jacket mixes elements from several military flight and cold-weather styles into one hybrid build.The hybrid coat takes the N-3B as its foundation, keeping the longer, cold-weather proportions of the original while adding details drawn from both the MA-1 and the CWU-45P. Combining three distinct references in one garment gives the coat a familiar military feel without tying it to any single archival piece.The hybrid flight jacket works the same idea in reverse. It keeps the shorter, instantly recognizable silhouette of the MA-1 and layers in details from the N-3B, bringing some of the parka’s practicality into a more compact flight-jacket shape.Both styles share the same technical foundation. Each is cut from a densely woven fabric treated with a water-repellent finish to handle wet conditions, while the interior is lined with WINDSTOPPER, a membrane that blocks wind while letting moisture escape. That pairing allows both jackets to protect against the elements without trapping heat and sweat inside.The White Mountaineering x Alpha Industries collaboration drops October 31 via White Mountaineering stores, the White Mountaineering online store and select stockists across Japan.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast
